content: Migrant and seasonal agricultural workers face significant barriers to accessing healthcare. These barriers include frequent migration, which disrupts continuity of care, and language difficulties that impede effective communication with healthcare providers. Additionally, their limited work hours and lack of familiarity with available healthcare resources further restrict their ability to seek and receive medical attention. As a result, these challenges contribute to reduced access to regular healthcare services, which increases the likelihood of severe and costly complications associated with diabetes. To address these issues, innovative care models such as mobile healthcare units and telehealth services can be implemented. These approaches aim to deliver healthcare directly to this population, overcoming logistical and systemic obstacles to care.
